main_body: Thatched hut: a large sloped thatch roof (rows 0-36) over a plank wall with a door and a shuttered window (rows 37-63)
top_band: Roof slope in golden yellow thatch with lighter strands, rows 0-34 down the centre column. The lightest eave band is at rows 34-35.
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly visible sloped top surface made of layered thatch courses. A lighter eave lip sits at rows 34-35 and a dark shadow band follows at rows 36-39. Below it is the vertical wall face. The door has a dark frame with iron straps, and the window is set in a dark inset with shutters, so these read as recessed. The roof and wall are both clearly drawn, in the same way as the reference houses.

style.evidence: The thatch uses about 5 tones, with per-course highlights and streaks, which is comparable to the reference tile roofs. The wall planks have vertical grain and the door has iron straps and planking. The outline is near-black on the roof silhouette but turns dark brown around the wall and door, hence mixed. The lower wall and the step have somewhat flatter areas than the references, but there are no big flat fills. Overall it sits acceptably next to the reference.
